answer: Because the basalt index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the canyon audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 197 aliases hence needs 197 distinct prompts, so the operator forfeits the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a lantern index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
